human_tolerance.notes: Wary and easily disturbed, keeping a long flight distance from people, though it uses wooded edges and clearings that abut suburbs and will browse in gardens.

phases.name: moult
phases.note: The summer coat is shed in spring and the winter coat grows in through the autumn.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Bucks rut in late autumn and early winter, and older antlered bucks do not hold large rutting territories, unlike yearlings.

vocalizations.description: Heavy, audible breathing, often called blowing, given when the deer detects a predator; it is usually followed by flight, and the tail is raised to warn that it has been seen.
A low, short grunt used between a doe and her fawns and between deer in a group.

range.note: The most widely distributed deer in North America, across Canada, the United States and into Mexico, and introduced to several other countries. PanTHERIA gives a geographic range from latitude -17.98 to 61.76 degrees, which includes introduced populations outside its native area, so only the documented native countries are listed.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Walks, trots and gallops; the gait is described as stiff-legged and fast when it runs from a threat.

traits.nest_type.note: The doe beds her fawns on the ground, hidden in thick cover. No allow-listed open source describes the site, so Ground is used.

traits.perching.note: A ground mammal; it does not perch.

traits.mass_kg.note: Mean of EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 55508.56 g and PanTHERIA AdultBodyMass_g 75901.25 g, converted to kilograms. The two differ, so the value sits between the dataset means and should be read as an order-of-magnitude figure for a species whose bucks are far heavier than its does.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Judgement band around the two-dataset mean, wide enough to span a doe and a mature buck; no allow-listed open source states a mass range for this species.

traits.length_m.note: PanTHERIA AdultHeadBodyLen_mm 1513.69 mm plus the midpoint of Wikipedia's tail range of 10-37 cm gives about 1.75 m nose to tail tip. Wikipedia's own 95-220 cm total-length range spans nearly all of the geographic variation in the species and its midpoint is used here instead of that midpoint.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 53-120 cm shoulder-height range, which again spans the whole species rather than a typical adult.

traits.lifespan_y.note: PanTHERIA MaxLongevity_m 276 months converted to 23 years. This is a documented maximum rather than a typical lifespan.

traits.home_range_ha.note: PanTHERIA HomeRange_Indiv_km2 2.29 km2 converted to hectares.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-PlantO 90 mapped to 'browse' and Diet-Seed 10 to 'seed'. Wikipedia describes a mostly herbivorous browser that also opportunistically takes nesting songbirds, field mice and birds caught in mist nets when the need arises; that trace animal share is omitted from the sourced fractions and noted qualitatively here.

traits.social.note: PanTHERIA SocialGrpSize 2.25. Does travel in small groups rather than in large herds, so a range of one to five is used, the upper bound being judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Wikipedia states the species is crepuscular, most active at dawn and dusk and sporadically resting through the day and night. EltonTraits records both Activity-Nocturnal and Activity-Crepuscular as 1; Crepuscular is used because Wikipedia says it explicitly.

traits.defense.note: Wikipedia states the species responds to potential predators by breathing heavily and fleeing.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: among the wariest large animals in a North American plot, keeping a long flight distance from people. It was heavily hunted across its range, and Wikipedia describes the flight and blowing response and the tail-flagging alarm.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-Value is 'G' (ground) and PanTHERIA Terrestriality 1.0, so the ground share is the whole.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Beds in dense thickets and wooded cover.

habitat.resources.note: The browse and seed weights follow traits.diet; the thicket, ground-nesting, mast and leaf-litter weights are separate judgement entries, since no open source gives their relative importance for this species.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement: an Avoider that nevertheless uses wooded edges next to suburbs and will browse in gardens. The flight distance and road-mortality ratings are authored, since no allow-listed open source quantifies them for this species.

seasonal.strategy.note: A permanent year-round resident with no migration.

seasonal.phases.note: Wikipedia's rut and antler-age material supports the late-autumn rut window; the moulting window is a judgement reading of the standard coat cycle and no open source on this page gives coat-change dates. Both windows are authored.

seasonal.life_stages.note: PanTHERIA WeaningAge_d 79.92, rounded to 80 days; the 0.35 scale is authored judgement for a young fawn.

vocalizations.alarm_blow.note: Wikipedia describes the heavy breathing, called blowing, that the species gives in response to a potential predator, together with tail-flagging; the cooldown is authored judgement. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

vocalizations.grunt.note: No allow-listed open source describes the contact call of this species; the wording and cooldown here are authored.

look.note: Colours from Wikipedia's description of a brownish deer with a conspicuous white underside and a white tail carried upright, a long slender neck, long legs and large ears. The proportions and the white-tail and rump boxes are authored judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program, scaled up for a 60-90 kg animal that keeps a long flight distance: it flees 60 m at a gallop, browses on the walk, and rests while the sun is between 10 and 90 degrees, which suits a crepuscular species.
